newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end up on higher growth forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end up on higher growth forecasts.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Thursday, as investors took positions ahead of second quarter corporate results due shortly, brokers said.
The all share index closed 5.5 points up at 810.8 points, with price gains outnumbering declines by 43 to 27. Ceylon Cold Stores closed five rupees up at 185, Lanka Lubricants two to 63.
"Since corporate results for the period to June 30, are expected to be good, investors are taking positions," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
Turnover was 252.7 million rupees, mainly due to nearly 500,000 shares of the blue chip Development Finance Corporation trading at 290 rupees a share.
"The market has more upside potential though the ride would be a bit bumpy due to profit-taking at regular intervals," said Derendra Abayaratna of The Unit Trust Management Co.

Brokers expect Friday to another good day, with the index gaining and turnover supported by the sale of 51 percent or 10.2 million shares of Malwatte Plantations, at a minimum price of 40 rupees a share. The government is privatising four more plantation firms, starting with Malwatte, through the stock exchange from July 4. --- Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
